{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My friend said her electricity was being shut off and she needed $500 immediately or her children would freeze. I emptied my emergency fund. A week later, she admitted her power was never at risk—she wanted to know if I was 'a real friend.' She returned the money, proud of my response.

CANDIDATE A:
My grandfather claimed the family farm was being foreclosed and only I could save it by moving back home. I quit my job and relocated. The farm was never in danger—he wanted to test whether I'd 'choose family over career.' He called my sacrifice 'the right answer.'

CANDIDATE B:
My friend called saying her electricity was being shut off and she needed $500 immediately for her children. I lent her the money. Later I saw the shutoff notice—it was real. She paid me back over the next few months as she got back on her feet. The need was genuine.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:52"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both stories involve a deceptive test of loyalty where the protagonist sacrifices significantly under false pretenses to prove their commitment, only to find out the situation was fabricated."}
